dataset: DS2: Esplora crawl of address histories for TxGPT, compact rows with hashed ids

steps: Read the tip height. Take 200 block heights spread evenly from tip - 52560 to tip - 100 (about the last 12 months).

From each block, take the output addresses of up to 4 pages of transactions; remove duplicates; remove every address in DS1's candidate pool (a superset of the DS1 addresses, so DS1 can never leak into TxGPT's training data).
Sort the pool, shuffle it with seed 30049, and visit candidates in that order.
Keep a candidate with 20-1000 confirmed transactions whose history passes every check. Stop once 4000 are kept (the minimum is 3000).
Worker threads finish in any order, so the last few kept addresses can differ between runs; the crawl may overshoot the target by up to the number of candidates in flight.

privacy: Addresses and txids appear only as salted SHA-256 prefixes. The salt (config/salt.txt) is not in the repository or the zip, so the ids cannot be linked back to addresses.

sources.pace: at most one request start every 0.5 s per host, 8 workers per host

reasons.too_few: fewer confirmed transactions than the minimum
reasons.too_many: more confirmed transactions than the maximum (busy services; a stated bias)
reasons.checks_failed: fetched, but an automated check failed
reasons.fetch_error: the API still returned an error after every retry

columns.addr_id: first hex characters of SHA-256(salt + address); the salt is not shipped
columns.txid_hash: first hex characters of SHA-256(salt + txid); used only to remove duplicates
columns.sent_sats: inputs spent from the address, satoshis (explorer/amounts.py)

list.name: row count equals tx_count for every address
list.detail: rows per addr_id against the visit's tx_count

list.name: no duplicate txid_hash within an address
no DS1 address in DS2
list.detail: 1533 pool addresses were in DS1's candidate pool and removed before the crawl

rebuild: python -m explorer.cli corpus   # resumes; a fresh crawl needs data/interim/corpus/ removed and gives different addresses
